text:
max: FYI saw a p95 jump ~11% after the kernel-selector tweak in the canary. Flamegraph points at host-side parse/tokenize hotspots. anyone else?
sophia: yup, reproducing locally. seems like extra memcpy in proto unpack and more small grpc writes.
kyle: can you paste the flame snippet?
max: here
```
flame: host::ingress::parse 48%
host::tokenize 22%
kernel_selector::score 6%
kvcache::lookup_miss 8%
grpc::writev 10%
```
lina: kvcache miss jump is suspicious — selector change may have altered prefix normalization so cache keys diverge.
raj: i also see an uptick in many small writes over http2 (hpack pressure) leading to syscall overhead. possible batching window too small.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 4550001000 -> 4550001100 rolled out to 20% at 2025-11-02T09:12:00Z
max: hypothesis: selector now prefers more medium-weight kernels which add host-side metadata ops; combined with proto packer tweak = parse CPU + increased writev frequency.
sophia: quick plan: revert selector scoring for 10m and measure p95, also collect kernel_choice_explain telemetry.
kyle: also try bumping batching window 4ms -> 12ms in dev to amortize TCP/syscall costs.
lina: i'll run a kvcache-diff job to compare key distributions before/after the change.
raj: i have a tiny repro for grpc fragmentation, sharing: 
```bash
# small script to create many small streaming chunks
python tests/stream_burst.py --chunk-size 128 --duration 60 --qps 200
```
max: run it against canary and baseline and grab tcpdump + strace.
sophia: also enable `kernel_choice_explain` metrics and collect ~5k requests for analysis.
kyle: if revert is not possible, interim mitigation = prefer compact kernels for short sequences and disable prefix normalization in selector.
lina: noted. i'll post results in a gist by EOD.
raj: ran the repro quickly — grpc writev syscalls doubled and p95 for ~512-token requests rose ~9% on canary.
sophia: if writev is the culprit, we can toggle sockopts (TCP_CORK) or adjust proxy writev-coalesce threshold. small wins.
max: also need to confirm tokenizer lib bump (v2.3) didn't change internal buffers causing memcpy hotspots.
deploy-bot: Rollback candidate ready: canary 4550001101 -> rollback to 4550001000. Please approve :thumbsup: 
kyle: +1 to rollback for safety; run experiments on staging before re-rolling.
lina: +1. pausing selector rollouts until we have kvcache diff.
raj: i'll add writev instrumentation to proxy for quick A/B.
sophia: action items: (1) rollback canary (max/kyle), (2) run kernel_choice_explain & kvcache-diff (lina/sophia), (3) run stream_burst on canary+baseline (raj), (4) try batching_window bump in dev (kyle). i'll draft a triage doc.
max: created triage doc https://docs.redwood/triage/4550001111 (will update with flamegraphs)
lina: flamegraphs uploaded: https://perf.redwood/fg/4550001111
max: thanks all — keep updates here, i'll track the rollback + perf runs.
